name: langchain-ai/langchain
checklist: The head branch is not `main` or `master` on the fork
A maintainer has assigned the linked issue to the submitting human
The description keeps `Fixes #NNNNN` as its first line
The title follows TYPE(SCOPE): DESCRIPTION, for example fix(core): ...
The pull request body is one or two sentences written by the submitting human
make format, make lint and make test pass in the modified package
The new test fails without the source change
notes: A bot closes any pull request whose linked issue is not assigned to its author, within hours and without review. Measured on 2026-09-03: 15 outside pull requests by humans merged in the previous fortnight, against 129 closed unmerged in the nine days to 2026-09-03.

A second bot rule: a pull request whose head branch is `main` or `master` on a fork is auto-closed, whatever else is true. #38640 was closed for this before the assignment check even ran. A branch named after the issue avoids it.

The assignment bot closes within minutes, not hours, and its comment says so in plain text: opening a pull request before assignment 'is discouraged and is not an indication that it will be accepted'. #38640, #38641 and #38647 were each closed the same minute they opened, so none of the three approaches on issue #38637 has ever been reviewed on merit. A pile of closed pull requests on a langchain issue is therefore not evidence that an approach was rejected.

Assignment is NOT reporter-only. #38351 was reported by Fr3ya, assigned to Sourav1331, and merged as #38355 on 2026-08-30. The earlier note that only a bug's reporter can win the assignment is contradicted by that row.
A linked issue is the norm, not an absolute. #39631, fix(core): make StructuredTool JSON-serializable, merged on 2026-08-27 from an outside author with no linked issue at all.
Assignment turnaround, where it happened, was fast: #39935, #39897 and #39895 were each reported, assigned to the reporter, fixed and merged within one to two days.
The template says a large, clearly AI-generated description may see the pull request ignored or closed. It says nothing against AI-assisted code.
The repository is a monorepo. Tests run per package under libs/, not from the root.

Because the enforcement bot mass-closes, a saturation screen that treats any referencing pull request as a claim reads this target as fully saturated. On 2026-09-03 that naive subtraction left 3 unassigned open bugs; counting only open or merged pull requests as a claim left 53.
